recognition: Recognized by Russia and a small number of other states; the EU supports Georgia’s internationally recognized borders.
provenance: Researched dossier. Each cited source has its own date; the newest citation is not a live verification of every field. No control geometry is inferred from areas of activity.

sources.title: EEAS: Statement on the thirty-third consolidated report on the conflict in Georgia
SIPRI: Major international armed conflicts, October 1993

name: Abkhazia
summary: Breakaway polity on Georgia’s Black Sea coast, supported by Russia. Georgia and most states regard the territory as part of Georgia.
military: De facto security structures with a Russian military presence.
origin: The 1992–1993 war separated the territory from Georgian central government control.
startBasis: 1993 marks consolidated de facto separation after war; constitutional and independence declarations have different dates.
